about: Based in Montreal, ccil shapes her sets around groove, tension, and acid touches; a sound she calls “deep groove,” both profound and groovy. She draws from raw & hypnotic techno, hardgroove, ghetto house & trance, building energy progressively while keeping space for surprise. Less interested in constant drops than in movement and pacing, she treats DJing as ongoing research: refining a personal language while staying attuned to the room and the shared energy of the dancefloor.

A member of T.I.T.S., a Montreal collective platforming FLINTA* artists, ccil is first and foremost a fan of underground dancefloors, which gave her spaces of freedom found nowhere else. Her sociological and political interests now lead her to organize: she wants to put tools in her community’s hands and sustain human bonds in spaces increasingly colonized by capitalist and patriarchal values. For her, art that doesn’t engage with the world is just entertainment, so she DJs and organizes in defense of freedom of assembly, and for the right of FLINTA* and queer people to gather, take up space, and be free.
